properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL.

For an epoch or increment that has ARRIVED there IS a past to point at, so the question is only which handle the graph stores. Three candidates, and they answer different questions rather than competing.

(a) GIT TAG (`epoch/2026-Q4`, `v0.18.0`). Human-readable, already the in-repo precedent — `rel:v0180` lives in the graph, tag `v0.18.0` lives in git, and nobody greps tags to learn what shipped. Cost: a tag is mutable and deletable, so a pin can quietly stop meaning what it meant.

(b) COMMIT SHA. Immutable and exact. Cost: opaque to a person, and says nothing about which repo it is in — useless on its own in a multi-repo ecosystem.

(c) THE EXPORT'S OWN `content_hash`. Every export already carries one, and `prev_content_hash` already chains them, so reflow2 HAS a version history of the design that owes git nothing. The same design exported on any machine hashes the same, which git cannot say of a commit. Cost: a hash identifies but does not LOCATE — you cannot fetch a document from its hash.

THE SHAPE THIS SUGGESTS: `content_hash` is the IDENTITY and the git ref is the ADDRESS. They answer "is this the same design?" and "where do I get it?", which are different questions, and storing both makes a third thing computable for free — if the tag later points at a commit whose export hashes differently, the pin has drifted, and that is exactly the kind of finding reflow2 exists to make rather than to suffer.

A SEPARATE QUESTION, and the one that decides how much is even needed: DOES REFLOW2 CREATE GIT REFS, OR ONLY RECORD THEM? Measured while thinking this through — reflow2 shells out to git NOWHERE. The merge driver is invoked BY git, never the reverse. So recording-only would preserve a property the tool currently has completely: it takes no clock, and it would take no VCS either. It could print the command it would have run. Creating tags would also mean write access to repos reflow2 does not own, which in an ecosystem of coupled repos is a different tool.

MULTI-REPO: one epoch does not pin one ref, it pins a SET — one per design — which is `req:version-combination-is-an-object`, already the recorded dependency of `req:epochs-can-be-planned`. So the pin is a version combination, not a string.
properties.name: OPEN — what identifies an arrived epoch's snapshot: a tag, a commit, or the export's own content hash?
properties.rationale:
Anthony's question (2026-07-30): how the mechanics of using git to capture snapshots would actually work. Recorded as options because he asked to think it through, not to be handed an answer.

The `content_hash` option is worth flagging because it was not in the original framing and it is already built: exports have carried `content_hash` and `prev_content_hash` since the lineage chain landed, and the gate already fails when the chain is broken. If identity is what is wanted, most of it exists.
